mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where PAYEMS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that may prompt the Federal Reserve to initiate monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO) and declining housing starts (HOUST) indicates a divergent economic landscape where manufacturing strength is offset by housing weakness, leading to increased market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where INDPRO increases and HOUST decreases month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a deceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL declining month-over-month) signals that the Federal Reserve's policy is effective without triggering a recession, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL declines, or the Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which typically supports economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where HOUST increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals economic weakness that may lead to a recession, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates effective monetary tightening that avoids a recession, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL declines month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 100), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals worsening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.
